title: fix(app-shell,console): zh names a Studio pillar by its tab label; settings label probes stop logging missing-translation warnings (objectui#11801)
body:
Fixes #11801
Clause-②: no

## Item 1: zh-CN names a Studio pillar by the label its tab shows

The pillar tab bar renders `t('engine.studio.pillar.KEY', locale)`, which reads 数据 / 自动化 / 界面 / 权限 in zh-CN. I enumerated every zh value of the designer tables, read through `readDesignerPairs` (the extractor `check:i18n-designer-parity` uses), for 支柱, or an English pillar name inside a value that holds Han text:

| Row (zh) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `engine.studio.nav.noObjects` | 这个软件包还没有对象 — 先到 Data 支柱创建。 | 这个软件包还没有对象 — 请先在「数据」中创建一个。 |
| `engine.studio.if.objectHintPre` | 运行态列表预览 · 改字段 / 结构请到 (trailing space) | 运行态列表预览 · 改字段 / 结构请到「 |
| `engine.studio.if.objectHintPost` | (leading space) 支柱 | 」 |

Two other rows matched the case-insensitive English probe but name no pillar: `engine.inspector.appNav.mode.filters` (a `/data` path) and `perm.posture.private.tip` (the `access.default` key). No other zh table in the file and nothing under `packages/i18n` says 支柱.

**One file outside the claim's file surface, changed in place.** The object-leaf hint's "Data" is not in the table. `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` rendered it as a literal span between `objectHintPre` and `objectHintPost`, so it read English in every locale whatever the zh rows said. The span now renders `t('engine.studio.pillar.data', locale)`, the key the tab bar renders, and en-US shows the same text as before. This uses the dispatch contract's bounded in-place exemption, and all four conditions hold:

- it is the card's defect class;
- it is a one-token change to the key the tab already uses;
- no in-flight claim holds that line (#11823 holds the inspector's studio-canvas branch; #11781, #11786, #11788 and #11792 hold the Data, Automations and Access regions and the save paths);
- it runs in the same gate family.

The seat should add that line to the claim's file surface.

The EN rows "create one in the Data pillar first" and "edit fields / structure in the Data pillar" already name the pillar by its en tab label, so no EN row changes.

## Item 2, the warnings: probes that fall back by design no longer log

`useSettingsLabel` finds a setting's label, help and option labels by probing `NS.settings.NAMESPACE.SUFFIX` in every top-level i18next namespace with a truthy `settings` member. On a miss it renders the manifest's own text. Each probe was a plain `t()` call, so each miss reached the dev missing-key handler in `@object-ui/i18n`.

I measured with the timezone row exactly as the server declares it (17 curated options), the built-in `en` pack resident, and the server's settings tree put through `transformSpecTranslations` (the console's own `loadLanguage` transform). Every warning came from one of two kinds of probe:

- **The four built-in namespaces that can never hold a settings tree.** `workspace.settings`, `sidebar.settings` and `user.settings` are menu-label strings, and `organization.settings` is the organization page's own strings. Every label, help and option probe into them misses.
- **`app.settings.localization.keys.timezone.options.ZONE`.** The server's en tree translates the timezone `label` and `help` but no option labels. That is by design: objectstack's settings-translation coverage test excludes option labels on purpose, so the manifest's option literal renders.

Neither kind is a missing translation. The triage direction "add the missing timezone keys to every locale that lacks them" has nothing to add: objectstack's `service-settings` translations carry `settings.localization.keys.timezone.label` and `.help` in all four locales it serves (en, zh-CN, ja-JP, es-ES).

The fix calls `i18n.exists(key)` before `t(key)`. `exists()` resolves through the same language and fallback chain and never reaches the missing-key handler, so what renders is unchanged. Inside `@object-ui/i18n`, `useObjectLabel` silences its own convention probes with an internal flag that the package does not export. The console cannot use that flag without widening a published surface.

The convention that stays is the one the hook already documents: `TranslationData.settings.NAMESPACE`, served by the server (under `app` after `transformSpecTranslations`), with the manifest literal as the fallback. No second home for settings labels is added.

## Item 2, the help wording: carried by objectstack-ai/objectstack#22136

The help line "IANA zone for today()/daysFromNow, analytics date buckets, and rendered datetimes." belongs to objectstack, not objectui:

- it is `settings.localization.keys.timezone.help` in `packages/services/service-settings/src/translations/en.ts`, served through `/api/v1/i18n/translations/en`;
- a near-copy is the `timezone` row's `description` in that package's `localization.manifest.ts`;
- zh-CN, ja-JP and es-ES carry the same developer wording.

An author-facing rewrite therefore belongs in objectstack, which this claim fences off. An objectui-side override would need a new `packages/i18n` key, widening the published `TranslationKeys`, and would give one setting's help a second home. The routes and the four-axis analysis are in the dev report on #11801.

**Seat ruling (A):** the rewrite belongs to objectstack's service-settings, the convention's one home. It is already filed and dispatched there as objectstack-ai/objectstack#22136 (open, `domain:services`). With that, objectui's share of #11801 is complete, so this PR closes it.

## Evidence

All test runs went from the repo root through the shared verify lock.

- **Item 2 pin, red first, then green.** `useSettingsLabel.conventionProbe-11801.test.tsx` on the `origin/main` source: 2 failed, 1 passed. After the fix: 3 passed. The red run captured the warnings: `label` and `help` for the four built-in namespaces, and every curated option in each discovered namespace.
- **Reverse checks from the committed fix.** Each mutation landed and was restored through `ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor count 1 → 0, blob changed; after restore the blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty):
  - Delete the `i18n.exists` gate: 2 failed, 1 passed (the two no-warning cases), as predicted.
  - Put the literal `Data` span back and keep the zh rows: 1 failed, 3 passed. The test received 「运行态列表预览 · 改字段 / 结构请到「Data」」.
  - Revert all four item-1 edits: 3 failed, 1 passed, as predicted. The offenders were `engine.studio.nav.noObjects` and `engine.studio.if.objectHintPost`; the en render was unchanged and stayed green.
- **Union at HEAD `3c268bb`:** 156 files and 1610 tests passed. `3c268bb` merges `origin/main` `456238c`, which carries objectui#11852 (`5d69133`) and its lowered eager-closure ceiling. The pre-merge run at `4143a03` read 149 files and 1538 tests. It covered the console settings directory, every app-shell test importing `StudioDesignSurface` or the metadata-admin `i18n` table, and the designer-parity and i18n-drift script suites.
- **Build:** `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/console^...' build` exited 0. This is the dependency closure, app-shell included.
- **Type-check:** `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell --filter @object-ui/console type-check` exited 0. `--listFilesOnly` shows both new test files in their package's type-check program.
- **Gates at HEAD `3c268bb`** (re-run after the merge; the closure build and both type-checks too), each exit 0: `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:i18n-designer-parity`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:shell-escape-residue` and `scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`.
- **Lint, narrowed and declared.** I ran eslint over the 5 touched TS/TSX files (population: eslint.config's `**/*.{ts,tsx}` blocks; count from `--format json`: 5). It found 0 errors and 13 warnings. All 13 are in `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`, the same count that file has at the merge base, and none is on the changed line. The config declares no `parserOptions.project`, and no rule under `eslint-rules/` reads another file, so the diff cannot change the verdict on any file it does not touch. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` runs in CI.

## Acceptance notes

- `resolveCommon` in `useSettingsLabel` (the source labels) also probes with plain `t()`. It only misses when a host serves a partial `settingsCommon`, and no served tree does today. Left as is.
- The `PILLARS` array in `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` still carries English `label` values that nothing renders; the tab bar reads `engine.studio.pillar.KEY`. Not changed.
- The header of objectstack's `service-settings` `translations/index.ts` says the console wires the settings bundle as `system`. The console actually reads it under `app` (through `/api/v1/i18n/translations`), and `useSettingsLabel` skips `system` by name. This is doc drift only, in another repo.
